question: Does XTestFakeDeviceKeyEvent, used by two separate X client connections opening the same server-provided XTEST virtual keyboard, preserve the core key state and focused-client KeyPress after client A sends UP while client B has not yet sent UP?
delta_from_existing_evidence: A05 tested sequential core XTEST versus InputOwner v10 for one client; existing analytical evidence models indistinguishable global keymaps. This new Xvfb run tests overlapping A/B holds on the same key for both core and device-specific XTEST APIs, checking whether the legacy device-specific entry point changes server-visible release behavior.

setup.socket_isolation: unshare --user --map-root-user --mount --propagation private; private tmpfs mounted over /tmp/.X11-unix

protocol.sink: focused core Xlib client selecting KeyPress and KeyRelease on one test window
protocol.device_api: XTestFakeDeviceKeyEvent using the same XTEST virtual keyboard id opened separately by connections A and B

decision.control_required: Core route keymap is neutral initially; down after A-DOWN and B-DOWN; after A-UP keymap is neutral and a matching KeyRelease reaches the focused core client while B has not sent UP; final state neutral.
decision.device_isolation_pass: Device route keymap stays down after A-UP and there is no matching core KeyRelease until B-UP; final state neutral.
decision.device_isolation_fail: Device route becomes neutral after A-UP and a matching core KeyRelease reaches the client while B has not sent UP; final state neutral.
decision.stop: Control, event receipt, API completion, keymap, target identity, cleanup, or Xvfb precondition is incomplete/inconsistent.

resource_scope: WSL Ubuntu process-local user/mount namespace; no Docker engine or GPU; one local Xvfb and four X client connections; no CPU/memory caps claimed.
limitations: shared server-provided XTEST virtual keyboard only
no production GUI/game or physical input
no model, useful feedback, recovery, task outcome, or safety claim
a positive result would require a distinct per-client virtual-device architecture and further testing
